title: finding(plugin-detail): `record:history` turns a refused row cap into `$top: 1` or a fractional window, while `record:activity` already refuses it
body:
`record:history` is the one renderer in the row-cap family that neither honours nor refuses a cap the contract rejects: it silently turns it into a one-row window or a fractional one. Its sibling `record:activity` already refuses-and-defaults. All readings below taken on `origin/main` at 2026-09-19T08:17Z, from source. ## The read point `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/record-history.tsx:76` ```ts const limit: number = Number(schema.limit ?? schema.properties?.limit ?? 50) || 50; ``` `:85` ```ts $top: Math.max(1, limit), ``` `||` rejects every falsy value, so `0`, `NaN` and `''` fall back to 50 — that part is fine. A **negative** is truthy, so it survives `||` and reaches `Math.max(1, …)`, which does not refuse it: it repairs it, to `1`. A **non-integer** is truthy too and `Math.max` passes it straight through to the wire. ## Measured, both renderers, same authored values Simulated from the two expressions verbatim (`record:history` `:76`+`:85`; `normalizeLimit` at `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/recordActivityFeed.ts:565`-`:567` with `DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_LIMIT = 20` at `:39`): | authored `limit`
all three columns read 2026-09-19T08:17Z on `origin/main` | `record:history` → `$top` | `record:activity` → window | |---|---|---| | absent | 50 | 20 | | `0` | 50 | 20 | | `-5` | **1** | 20 | | `2.5` | **2.5** | 2 | | `'lots'` | 50 | 20 | | `10` | 10 | 10 | The last row is the control: a usable cap passes through unchanged on both, so the substitutions above are readings rather than a dead harness. `record:activity`'s column is not merely observed — it is pinned, at `packages/plugin-detail/src/renderers/__tests__/recordActivityFeed.test.ts:431`-`:436` (`normalizeLimit(0)`, `(-3)`, `(undefined)` and `('lots')` all assert `DEFAULT_ACTIVITY_LIMIT`). Nothing pins `record:history`'s. What would make these not be these values: an earlier guard on `schema.limit` before `:76`. There is none — `:76` is the only derivation, and `$top: Math.max(1, limit)` at `:85` is the only consumer. ## Why this is a contract question, not a taste one `@objectstack/spec` declares every member in this family a **positive integer** (`z.number().int().positive().optional()`). `-5` and `2.5` are values the contract refuses. A renderer may refuse them loudly or accept them, but `record:history` does neither: it rewrites `-5` into a window of 1 and forwards `2.5` to the adapter as a fractional `$top`, and says nothing either way. The author sees one row, or an unpredictable one, and no cause is named. This is the `declared` ≠ `enforced` shape, and the family now holds two answers to one question: `record:activity` refuses and defaults; `record:history` clamps. objectui#9925 is landing the refuse-and-warn answer at three more read points (`object-kanban`, `object-timeline`, `record:reference_rail`), which leaves `record:history` as the only member still clamping. ## ⛔ Correction to a note already published PR objectui#10001's `## Acceptance notes` states that for `record:history` and `record:activity` "an authored `0` there still becomes a window of 1 in silence." That is wrong on both halves and the table above is why: `0` becomes **50** in `record:history` (the `||` catches it) and **20** in `record:activity`, and `record:activity` never clamps at all. The defect is real but its trigger is a negative or a non-integer, in `record:history` only. The PR body is being corrected in place. ## Scope note Bringing `record:history` onto the family's answer is an execution step once someone rules which answer the family keeps. Deciding that — refuse-and-warn everywhere, or clamp everywhere — is not an execution step, which is why this is filed rather than appended to objectui#10001. Dedupe words: `record-history limit negative $top` · `plugin-detail Math.max(1, limit)` · `record-history row cap clamp` · `normalizeLimit record-history parity` · `fractional $top record history` --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_
